what_its_for: Aclidinium is a long-acting bronchodilator (airway opener) used to treat chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), including chronic bronchitis and emphysema. It helps relax and widen the airways in your lungs, making it easier to breathe. It is a maintenance (long-term, daily) medication and is NOT meant to treat sudden breathing problems or asthma attacks.
how_to_take: Aclidinium comes as a dry powder inhaler. Here is how to use it: 1) Remove the protective cap by squeezing the arrows on the sides. 2) Hold the inhaler with the mouthpiece facing you and the green button on top. 3) Press the green button all the way down, then release it. You will hear a click. 4) Check the control window — it should turn GREEN, meaning a dose is ready. If it is still red, press the button again. 5) Breathe out fully away from the inhaler (do not blow into it). 6) Place the mouthpiece in your mouth, close your lips tightly around it, and breathe in FAST and DEEPLY. 7) Remove the inhaler from your mouth and hold your breath for 5 to 10 seconds. 8) Breathe out slowly. 9) Check the control window again — if it turned RED, you got your full dose. If it is still GREEN, repeat the inhalation step. 10) Replace the protective cap. Do NOT shake the inhaler. Do NOT wash the mouthpiece with water.
dosing: The usual dose is ONE inhalation (400 micrograms) TWICE a day — once in the morning and once in the evening, about 12 hours apart. Try to take it at the same times each day. Do not take more than 2 inhalations in 24 hours.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — BUT only if your next scheduled dose is more than 6 hours away. If it is less than 6 hours until your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store the inhaler at room temperature between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not freeze. Keep the protective cap on when not in use. The inhaler has a dose counter — when it shows '0', it is empty and you need a new one. Discard it 45 days after opening the foil pouch or when the dose counter reads '0', whichever comes first.
what_to_avoid: Do not use aclidinium as a rescue inhaler during a sudden COPD flare-up or breathing emergency — always keep a separate fast-acting (rescue) inhaler such as albuterol on hand for emergencies. Avoid getting the powder in your eyes. Tell your doctor before using if you take other anticholinergic medications (such as tiotropium or ipratropium), as combining them may increase side effects. Avoid using if you are allergic to aclidinium or any of its ingredients.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or get emergency help RIGHT AWAY if you experience: sudden worsening of breathing or wheezing after using the inhaler (paradoxical bronchospasm); chest pain or fast/irregular heartbeat; difficulty urinating or pain when urinating (signs of urinary retention); eye pain, blurred vision, or seeing halos around lights (signs of increased eye pressure — narrow-angle glaucoma); severe allergic reaction signs such as rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty swallowing. Also call your doctor if your COPD symptoms are not well controlled or getting worse.
when_it_works: Aclidinium starts to open your airways within about 30 minutes after your first dose. However, the full benefit builds up over several days of regular use. You should notice it becomes easier to breathe during daily activities over time. Remember, this medication works best when taken every day, even when you feel well.
special_populations: Older adults (65 years and older): Aclidinium can generally be used safely in older adults at the same dose. However, older patients may be more sensitive to side effects such as constipation, dry mouth, or urinary problems. Kidney or liver problems: No dose adjustment is needed for mild to moderate kidney or liver disease. Tell your doctor if you have severe kidney or liver disease. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: It is not known if aclidinium is safe during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Talk to your doctor before using if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Children: Aclidinium is NOT approved for use in children or teenagers. COPD is primarily a condition in adults.
